== History ==
== Founding ==
The date of founding is unknown. According to the “Inadahime-no-Miya Shrine Origin” ({{ill|Edo period|Q184963|qid=Q184963}}), when a servant of the local village headman Takemochi went to draw water from the Inada Yoshii spring, a woman appeared beside the spring. When Takemochi went to ask about her after being informed by the servant, she replied, “I am Kushinada-hime, the local tutelary deity of this land.” She then delivered a divine message instructing that shrines be built for her parents and for her as a married couple, and that rice be cultivated with the water of the Yoshii spring and worshipped accordingly<ref name="神々"/>. About 300 meters northwest of the shrine, on the mid-slope of Mount Inada, stands the main sanctuary (Okunoin). To the left of its small shrine, a massive rock juts out; this {{ill|Iwakura rock|Q11587880|qid=Q11587880}} is said to be the site where Inada-hime descended to earth<ref name="神々"/>.

It is also believed that the shrine was worshipped by the {{ill|Niihari no Kuni no Miyatsuko|Q11502674|qid=Q11502674}}<ref name="神々"/>. The Niihari no Kuni no Miyatsuko were {{ill|Kuni no miyatsuko|Q2483673|qid=Q2483673}} who are said to have ruled the {{ill|Niihari District, Ibaraki|Q5765974|qid=Q5765974}} area before the {{ill|Ritsuryō|Q742460|qid=Q742460}}. In the “{{ill|Kujiki|Q2716751|qid=Q2716751}}” under the “{{ill|Kokuzo Hongi|ja|国造本紀|qid=Q133833194}}” entry for Niihari no Kuni no Miyatsuko, it is recorded that Hinarafu no Mikoto, son of Mitoroki no Mikoto, was the first to hold the office. Mitoroki no Mikoto (also read Mitsurogi no Mikoto) was an eighth-generation descendant of {{ill|Ame no Hohi|fr|Clan Izumo|ja|出雲国造|simple|Izumo clan|qid=Q11395856|lt=Ame-no-Hohi}} and shared ancestry with the {{ill|Izumo clan|fr|Clan Izumo|ja|出雲国造|simple|Izumo clan|qid=Q11395856}}. In the area around this shrine are several {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}}—{{ill|Sashino Shrine|ja|佐志能神社|qid=Q27500771}}, {{ill|Kamo-Ōkami-miko-kami-nushi-tama Shrine|Q66085127|qid=Q66085127}}, and {{ill|Okunitama Shrine|ja|大国玉神社 (桜川市)|qid=Q11433665|lt=Ōkunitama Shrine}}—all of which enshrine deities of Izumo lineage, leading scholars to point out connections with the historical records<ref name="神々"/>.

== Overview ==
There are no references to this shrine in official histories such as the {{ill|Rikkokushi|Q1151168|qid=Q1151168}}<ref name="神々"/>. However, in the mid-{{ill|Heian period|Q193292|qid=Q193292}}, the “{{ill|Engishiki|ar|إنجيشيكي (كتاب ياباني)|de|Engishiki|es|Engishiki|fr|Engishiki|he|אנגישיקי|id|Engishiki|it|Engishiki|ja|延喜式|ko|엔기시키|min|Engishiki|mr|इंगिशिकी|nl|Engishiki|pt|Engishiki|ru|Энгисики|simple|Engishiki|tr|Engishiki|uk|Енґісікі|zh|延喜式|qid=Q1342448}}” {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932|lt=Register of Deities}} lists “Inada Shrine, Myōjin Taisha” in {{ill|Hitachi Province|Q1055353|qid=Q1055353}}, {{ill|Niihari District, Ibaraki|Q5765974|qid=Q5765974}}, ranking it as a {{ill|Myōjin Taisha|Q9610964|qid=Q9610964}}.

In the early {{ill|Kamakura period|Q236205|qid=Q236205}}, the local lord {{ill|Tokitomo Kasama|ja|笠間時朝|qid=Q11599988}} invited eight poets including {{ill|Hamuro Mitsutoshi|es|Hamuro Mitsutoshi|it|Hamuro Mitsutoshi|ja|葉室光俊|qid=Q23613350|lt=Fujiwara no Mitsutoshi}} and {{ill|Yasutsuna|ja|宇都宮泰綱|qid=Q11449785|lt=Yasutsuna}} to hold a poetry offering gathering at the shrine. The poems from this event are recorded in the “Shin Wakashū” (Utsunomiya Shin Wakashū)<ref name="地名"/>.

At the end of the {{ill|Muromachi period|Q334845|qid=Q334845}}, the shrine buildings were destroyed by warfare. In {{ill|Keichō|Q1328185|qid=Q1328185}} 7 ({{ill|1602|ab|1602|af|1602|als|1602|am|1602 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|1602|ar|1602|ary|1602|arz|1602|ast|1602|avk|1602|az|1602|azb|۱۶۰۲ (میلادی)|ban|1602|bar|1602|bcl|1602|be|1602|be_x_old|1602|bg|1602|bn|১৬০২|bpy|মারি ১৬০২|br|1602|bs|1602.|ca|1602|cdo|1602 nièng|ceb|1602|ckb|١٦٠٢|crh|1602|cs|1602|csb|1602|cv|1602|cy|1602|da|1602|de|1602|diq|1602|el|1602|eml|1602|eo|1602|es|1602|et|1602|eu|1602|fa|۱۶۰۲ (میلادی)|fi|1602|fo|1602|fr|1602|frr|1602|fur|1602|fy|1602|ga|1602|gan|1602年|gcr|1602|gd|1602|gl|1602|he|1602|hi|१६०२|hr|1602.|hsb|1602|ht|1602 (almanak gregoryen)|hu|1602|hy|1602|hyw|1602 թուական|ia|1602|id|1602|ilo|1602|io|1602|is|1602|it|1602|ja|1602年|jv|1602|ka|1602|kaa|1602|kk|1602 жыл|kn|೧೬೦೨|ko|1602년|krc|1602 джыл|ksh|Joohr 1602|la|1602|lb|1602|lez|1602 йис|li|1602|lij|1602|lmo|1602|lt|1602 m.|lv|1602. gads|mai|१६०२|map_bms|1602|mdf|1602|mg|1602|mhr|1602|mi|1602|mk|1602|mr|इ.स. १६०२|mrj|1602 и|ms|1602|my|၁၆၀၂|mzn|۱۶۰۲|nah|1602|nap|1602|nds|1602|new|सन् १६०२|nl|1602|nn|1602|no|1602|nrm|1602|nso|1602|oc|1602|or|୧୬୦୨|os|1602-æм аз|pl|1602|pnb|1602|pt|1602|qu|1602|ro|1602|ru|1602 год|rue|1602|sa|१६०२|sah|1602|scn|1602|sd|1602ع|se|1602|sh|1602.|shn|1602|simple|1602|sk|1602|sl|1602|smn|1602|sq|1602|sr|1602|su|1602|sv|1602|sw|1602|szl|1602|ta|1602|te|1604|tg|Соли 1602|th|พ.ศ. 2145|tk|1602|tl|1602|tly|1602|tr|1602|tt|1602 ел|uk|1602|ur|1602ء|uz|1602|vec|1602|vi|1602|vls|1602|wa|1602|war|1602|wuu|1602年|xmf|1602|yi|1602|zh|1602年|zh_min_nan|1602 nî|zh_yue|1602年|qid=Q6727}}), when {{ill|Ina Tadatsugu|de|Ina Tadatsugu|fa|اینا تاداتسوگو|fr|Ina Tadatsugu|it|Ina Tadatsugu|ja|伊奈忠次|ko|이나 다다쓰구|zh|伊奈忠次|qid=Q3387913}} conducted a land survey of the area, the main hall and other structures were rebuilt<ref name="地名">“Place Names of Ibaraki Prefecture,” entry on Inada Shrine.</ref>. In {{ill|Kanbun (era)|es|Kanbun|fa|کانبون (دوره)|fr|Ère Kanbun|id|Kanbun (era)|ja|寛文|ko|간분|ru|Камбун (нэнго)|simple|Kanbun (era)|sr|Канбун (ера)|sv|Kanbun|tr|Kanbun (dönem)|zh|寬文|qid=Q1146228}} 8 ({{ill|1668|Q7595|qid=Q7595}}), the domain lord Inoue Masatoshi granted the shrine four koku of tax-exempt land<ref name="地名"/>. In {{ill|Genroku|Q1325001|qid=Q1325001}} 7 ({{ill|1694|Q7694|qid=Q7694}}), {{ill|Tokugawa Mitsukuni|Q1194944|qid=Q1194944}} visited the shrine, lamented the decline of the ancient sanctuary, and dedicated origin records and other items (the shrine treasure of the Four Guardian Deity Banners was dedicated in Genroku 11 ({{ill|1698|Q7706|qid=Q7706}}))<ref name="四神旗"/>. The shrine buildings burned down again in {{ill|Kōka|Q1325317|qid=Q1325317}} 2 ({{ill|1845|Q7636|qid=Q7636}}) and were rebuilt in {{ill|Kaei|Q1146125|qid=Q1146125}} 1 ({{ill|1848|Q7647|qid=Q7647}})<ref name="地名"/>.

In the {{ill|Meiji era|ar|فترة مييجي|ast|Dómina Meiji|az|Meydzi dövrü|azb|مئی‌جی دؤورو|be|Перыяд Мэйдзі|bn|মেইজি যুগ|bo|མེའི་ཇིའི་དུས་དུས་མཚམས།|ca|Era Meiji|cs|Období Meidži|da|Meiji-perioden|de|Meiji-Zeit|el|Μεϊτζί (περίοδος)|es|Era Meiji|et|Meiji periood|eu|Meiji Aroa|fa|دوره میجی|fi|Meiji-kausi|fr|Ère Meiji|gl|Período Meiji|he|תקופת מייג'י|hr|Meiji (razdoblje)|ht|Epòk Meiji|hu|Meidzsi-kor|id|Zaman Meiji|io|Ero Meiji|is|Meiji-tímabilið|it|Periodo Meiji|ja|明治|ka|მეიძის ეპოქა|kbp|Mejii wɛɛ yaa alɩwaatʊ|kk|Мэйдзи дәуірі|ko|메이지 시대|la|Aetas Meiji|lt|Meidži laikotarpis|lv|Meidzi periods|mk|Меиџи (период)|mn|Мэйжийн эрин|ms|Zaman Meiji|nl|Meijiperiode|nn|Meiji|no|Meiji-perioden|pl|Meiji (okres)|pt|Era Meiji|ro|Perioada Meiji|ru|Мэйдзи|simple|Meiji period|sk|Obdobie Meidži|sq|Periudha Meixhi|sr|Меиџи период|sv|Meijiperioden|ta|மெய்சி காலம்|th|ยุคเมจิ|tl|Panahong Meiji|tr|Meiji Dönemi|uk|Період Мейдзі|ur|میجی دور|vi|Thời kỳ Minh Trị|war|Panahon Meiji|wuu|明治|zh|明治|zh_classical|明治|zh_min_nan|Bêng-tī|zh_yue|明治|qid=Q3125096}}, under the {{ill|Q712534|lt=Modern shrine ranking system}}, the shrine was designated a {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Prefectural shrine}}.

== Subsidiary and auxiliary shrines ==
'''Shrines within the grounds'''
* Tenazuchi Shrine (てなづちじんじゃ)
** Enshrined deity: {{ill|Ashinazuchi and Tenazuchi|Q643763|qid=Q643763|lt=Tenazuchi no Mikoto}}
*: The “father shrine” of the “parents’ shrine” mentioned in the origin legend; located to the front left of the worship hall.
* Ashinazuchi Shrine (あしなづちじんじゃ)
** Enshrined deity: {{ill|Ashinazuchi and Tenazuchi|Q643763|qid=Q643763|lt=Ashinazuchi no Mikoto}}
*: The “mother shrine” of the “parents’ shrine” mentioned in the origin legend; located to the front right of the worship hall.
* Yakumo Shrine
** Enshrined deity: {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|Q272993|qid=Q272993|lt=Susanoo no Mikoto}}
*: The “husband shrine” of the “married couple shrine” mentioned in the origin legend; located to the right of the main hall.
In addition, several other shrines stand within the grounds.

<gallery>
File:Inada-jinja (Kasama) Tanazuchi-jinja.JPG|Tenazuchi Shrine
File:Inada-jinja (Kasama) Ashinazuchi-jinja.JPG|Ashinazuchi Shrine
File:Inada-jinja (Kasama) Yakumo-jinja.JPG|Yakumo Shrine
</gallery>

'''Shrines outside the grounds'''
* Main sanctuary (Okunoin)
*: Located about 300 meters northwest of the main shrine on the mid-slope of Mount Inada ({{Coord|36|22|15.59|N|140|12|12.91|E|region:JP-08_type:landmark|name=Main sanctuary (Okunoin)}}). It is said to be the shrine’s former original site.

== Festivals ==
* First prayer ceremony (January 1)<ref>Festival information based on explanatory signs within the shrine grounds.</ref>
* Setsubun Festival (February 3) – held on the 4th in leap years
* Kinen Festival (February 19)
* Gion Festival (July 30)
*: A grand festival based on the legend that Susanoo no Mikoto reunited with Kushinada-hime no Mikoto at the site of the main sanctuary; the portable shrine spends one night at the Okunoin<ref name="神々"/>.
* Grand annual festival (November 17)

== Cultural properties ==
== Tangible Cultural Property designated by Ibaraki Prefecture ==
* Four Guardian Deity Banners (4 streamers) (historical materials)
*: Dedicated in {{ill|Genroku|Q1325001|qid=Q1325001}} 11 ({{ill|1698|Q7706|qid=Q7706}}) by {{ill|Tokugawa Mitsukuni|Q1194944|qid=Q1194944}}. They depict the Four Guardian Beasts: Azure Dragon (East), White Tiger (West), Vermilion Bird (South), and Black Tortoise (North). In the lower right of the banners is the inscription: “Respectfully dedicated Four Guardian Banners, Jōshū Niihari District Inada Shrine, Genroku year, Minamoto Mitsukuni.” Designated on January 25, Showa 63 (1988)<ref name="四神旗">[http://www.city.kasama.lg.jp/index.php?code=331 Four Guardian Deity Banners] (Kasama City website).</ref>.
